newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - March 24.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.

- The Irish general election started unofficially on Sunday when the main opposition party, Fianna Fail, began an eight-week advertising campaign and the Minister for Justice, Nora Owen, accused Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern of "having no creditability on crime."

- A major security operation was underway early on Monday at the high-security Maze prison in Northern Ireland, after the discovery of a tunnel leading from a block housing Provision Irish Republican Army inmates.
- Irish police investigating the recent murder of two women in Dublin have called in British experts in drafting psychological profiles of serial killers.
- The Grand Master of the Orange Order is denying his organisation is split over the issue of compromising on controversial parades in the forthcoming marching season.

- An attack on a prostitute by a man in a hijacked taxi may hold the key to the savage murder of two elderly women in Dublin. - Ireland's coalition government is planning a huge pre-election jobs announcement as ministers prepare for the campaign trail. - Satellite network Sky Television is planning a specialised Irish "pub channel" showing sporting events which won't be available to householders.
- Irish companies are becoming "greener" or at least taking steps to become more environmentally friendly, according to the results of a survey of 500 Irish employers.
- Irish police investigating the murders of two women in Dublin
fear the killer may have eaten body parts that he cut off the victims.
- Ireland's aspirant home-buyers are to be faced with still higher prices over the coming decade.

- Angry residents warned on Sunday they would erect barriers and physically prevent death riders from driving through their neighbourhoods as the fury continued to mount in the wake of last week's double fatality involving a stolen car.
